statement: There is no computer control for many weak enemies: henchmen are paper only, the one-versus-many director (the ring) is parked and not on main, and a match holds five bodies at most with no waves or respawn.
depends_on: F-MODES-02 (the horde design page comes first)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable with a recorded token cost; the parked ring is 503 lines of director code plus edits to seven director files for one fighter with up to four guards, and a horde needs grades, waves and respawn on top (the whole mode is costed XL in F-MODES-02; this row is the enemy control only)
risk: The parked ring was built for one boss with strong guards, not a swarm; reusing it may not fit and its exact-text patches are a month old. Early sign: the patch scripts stop at the first missing anchor.

statement: Easy is too hard for a scripted player using Orb's scheme: it won 19 of 40 (47.5%) on the tree that became the played build, against Game Design's band of at least 70% and the criterion's proposed 60 to 80%.
cost_basis: estimate; comparable: the pace-match and hit-stop row re-reads were each a handful of 40-match cells on data levers (docs/director/runs/6eec6a75/hitstop-row/), no token cost recorded
risk: Tuning Easy for the scripted pad may make it trivial for a button masher (the masher read 17 of 40 on the same cell); read both pads each time.

statement: Medium and Hard have no win-rate record for Orb's scheme on any build since 2026-11-01; the only figures on a design page are 0 wins at each level from 10 matches.
cost_basis: estimate; six cells of 40 matches with the existing gauntlet (the hit-stop row ran eight such cells in one job)
risk: If Medium and Hard are near 0% for a guarding player, the three levels are not distinct for the people Alpha is for; one batch shows it.

statement: No win rate has been measured on the played build's own packed data: every record was made on a scratch tree with patches laid on, by a Tools script that is not in QA's folder or in CI.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the player and the level option exist, what is missing is a run against a build's tree/data and a saved record under docs/qa/runs/<sha>/
risk: A build's switch list can differ from the tree a batch ran on; without a packed-data run the Alpha candidate's difficulty is unknown.

statement: Main's computer-opponent data is not the played build's: Easy's pace matching, the beam pacing against a human, and the computer's hold-and-release beam are on in the build and off on main.
cost_basis: estimate; three data keys and a golden re-record, the same kind of job as F-MODES-08
risk: A candidate built from main without the switch page gives Easy 12-tick strings, which read 2 of 40 for Orb's scheme (record:docs/director/runs/397a7adf/pace-match/gauntlet/gauntlet_cells.txt:4, uncommitted).

statement: The computer never throws a right-stick strike, the main attack of Orb's scheme: the only right-stick input the computer writes is the beam's hold.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; a new choice in the computer's brawl and band input with per-level rates, then a re-read of every level's win rate
risk: Adding stuns and placement blows to the computer moves every win rate; do it before the X-06 bands are tuned, not after.
orb_question: Must the computer use the right-stick strikes in Alpha? Recommendation: yes at Medium and Hard, after the horde's enemy control and before the final difficulty tuning.

statement: No standing check proves the computer uses only inputs a player has: on main its signature is still the old B request that locks its rival, the hold-and-release check is local only, and no record of it exists for the played build.
cost_basis: estimate; QA's beam trace exists (the criterion's own note) and needs a count of computer beams by starting input, plus a CI row for beam_ai_check
risk: Orb's complaint of 2026-11-06 (the computer charging beams in melee range) has no after-the-fix record; it could return unnoticed with any switch change.

statement: There is no computer ally: the only 2v2 line-up puts both computers on the enemy team, and no menu or host can start a match with a computer on a human's side.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the partner behaviours exist for any computer slot, so the work is a line-up, a measured quality bar and the check in CI
risk: An ally that plays at the enemy's level (see F-AI-10) either carries the player or is useless; nothing measures it today.

statement: Matches against Easy run long: the scripted Orb's-scheme player's 40 matches averaged about 576 seconds and the masher's about 426, against the criterion's normal match of 6 to 8 minutes.
cost_basis: estimate; a read of match length beside each win-rate cell (the gauntlet already saves each match's length)
risk: A first match of nearly ten minutes that the newcomer loses half the time is where a tester stops; lengths fall as Easy is tuned, so read them together.

statement: The computer's level is one value for the whole match, not one per fighter, so an ally weaker or stronger than the enemy, or graded enemies, cannot be set.
cost_basis: estimate; the data file's own note calls it "step 4", a per-slot setup key, with about ten read sites of DirAI.level in sim/director
risk: Left until the horde or the ally is built, it becomes a rewrite under both; cheap now.

statement: The fix for Orb's remark that the computer perfect-blocks charged attacks too easily is parked and not on main: its data key is in the schema but in no data file and no code.
cost_basis: estimate; the probe exists (qa/godot/charge.gd) and the park was one script on two director files, but its anchors date from 2026-10-16 and need a re-cut
risk: The measured rate on 2026-10-16 was about 6% of charged heavies, all decided before the release; the feeling Orb reported may come from when it happens, not how often, so measure on the played build before re-cutting.

statement: The checks of the computer opponent run by hand only: the level check, the pace check, the computer-beam check and the 2v2 partner check are not in CI, and no CI job reads a win-rate band.
cost_basis: estimate; four short headless rows added to an existing CI job (win-rate batches are too long for CI and stay a saved record)
risk: A level that silently reads another level's numbers, or pace matching that stops working, would not be seen until someone plays.

statement: Forty matches a cell cannot tell neighbouring bands apart (about 15 points either way), and the drop the EP flagged, 65% to 45% for Easy, is inside that noise and was read on two different trees.
cost_basis: estimate; a change of the criterion's sample size and one re-run of the two trees on the same seeds
risk: Tuning to a 40-match reading chases noise; the bands in X-06 are 20 points wide, the same size as the error.

statement: Backburnered ideas are still in the computer's decisions: it picks where to lead the fight from the hero and villain meters, and its hiding choices remain in code though no fighter can hide.
cost_basis: estimate; a ruling (keep, re-key to the fighter's role, or retire) and a small edit with a golden re-record
risk: A third fighter with neither meter would not roam at all (location.gd:104-105), which is fighter-specific behaviour hidden in old data.

statement: Some of the computer's numbers are constants in code, not data: how often an attack beat attacks, the share of heavies, and the blind swing.
risk: Low; these apply to every level alike, so the levels cannot differ on them without a code change.

statement: The scripted Orb's-scheme player is a narrow model of the scheme: right-stick flicks and a held LB guard only, and it fired no beam in 40 matches while Easy fired 459.
cost_basis: estimate; the gauntlet's beam arm already holds RB and the stick, so a combined arm is small
risk: Bands tuned to a pad with no beam, signature, dash or transformation will be too easy for a real player who uses them.

statement: The parked one-versus-many work was last rebuilt on 2026-10-16 and applies by exact-text patches; whether it still applies to today's director code is not evidenced.
cost_basis: estimate; the README's own check mode for a sibling park reads every anchor and writes nothing, so a dry run is one command for the owner
risk: A horde plan that counts on the ring may find the patches dead; a dry run settles it before the design page is written.

statement: Three levels exist in data and differ on 83 values, the start menu offers them, and the chosen level travels in the match setup and the replay header.

Easy's pace matching is built and on in the played build: its strings are never quicker than the player's own recent presses, between 12 and 30 ticks, and it lifted the scripted pad from 2 to 26 wins of 40.
In the played build the computer's beams, its signature included, go through the same hold and release of the right stick as a player's.
The computer acts only by writing the same input record a player's pad writes, and its perfect-block chance is data per level with a separate, lower rate for a heavy it sees wound up.
A scripted player for Orb's scheme exists and takes a level: right-stick flicks at thumb pace with LB held from the rival's wind-up to contact.

2v2 partner behaviours are built for any computer fighter: it flies to the other fight when its own is done, comes when its partner is on the brink, and dodges a beam from the other fight; the check passed on 20713b02.
The sim's first stage of one versus many is on main: a match holds two to five bodies and only the first two decide it.
